chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat and Abdullah ibn Jabalat, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had children, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man for the absent one from his father? He said: 'It is set aside until he comes.' I said: 'So upon his wealth is Zakat?' He said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'So if he comes, does he purify it?' He said: 'No, until a year passes with it being in his hand.' So I said: 'The man is lost and does not come?' He said: 'If the inheritors of the man are reliable with his wealth, they distribute it among themselves. So whenever he comes, they return it to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the inheritance and Zakat of a missing person whose whereabouts are unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential handling of a missing heir (al-gha'ib), establishing that his share is segregated and exempt from Zakat until his return, with distribution to other heirs only if he remains absent. It highlights the Shia principle of preserving the missing person's rights while allowing estate liquidity, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to inheritance disputes. The ruling underscores the balance between finality in estate settlement and the potential for restitution upon the heir's reappearance.
